system_prompt_style.note: Two prompts (pre-allocation, reallocation) filled with system state.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: The IDA receives the request and queries its internal database for current system status (all user states, total available bandwidth)
env_context_strategy.note: Network state injected from DB, not a repository/file-tree environment; no navigation tools.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: Read user requests one by one from the user queue file (Tables/user_configs.json).
context_compaction.note: No condenser/truncation mechanism described; each user handled with fresh prompts.

observation_format.evidence_quote:
Output Format:
JSON object with allocated resources.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote:
Output Format:
JSON object with original vs. modified user configs.
tool_call_format.note: LLM emits JSON configurations parsed by the harness; no function-calling API evidence.

tool_count.evidence_quote: we realize IDA as an LLM-based agent composed of two principal routines: (1) bandwidth pre-allocation and (2) bandwidth reallocation
tool_count.note: No tool schemas exposed to the model; the LLM only returns JSON configurations.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: RDA Execution: The user-side RDA receives the configuration parameters from the IDA and processes/transmits its data accordingly.
edit_primitive.note: No file-editing capability in the framework.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: prompts.py               # Contains the prompt templates for interacting with the LLM.
tool_schema_source.note: No tool schemas; prompt templates are hand-authored.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: pip install torch torchvision pandas tqdm openai

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: The IDA employs a two-stage planning scheme (bandwidth pre-allocation and reallocation)
loop_primitives.note: Reallocation stage repeats until sufficient bandwidth or no adjustments possible.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote:
CoT Path:
1.Select model config based on QoS.
2.Select code rate based on SNR.
3.Calculate required bandwidth.
4.Verify if bandwidth is sufficient.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: we propose RIDAS, a multi-agent framework composed of representation-driven agents (RDAs) and an intention-driven agent (IDA)
multi_agent_topology.note: IDA (LLM) configures RDAs (non-LLM model agents); hand-off is fixed IDA->RDA.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: The user-side RDA receives the configuration parameters from the IDA and processes/transmits its data accordingly.
delegation_mechanism.note: IDA passes control parameters to RDAs; no agent spawning.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: Read user requests one by one from the user queue file (Tables/user_configs.json).
human_in_loop.note: Fully automated simulation loop; no approval step.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: The memory module of IDA persistently stores the current configuration set, i.e., the control parameters of all connected RDAs

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: experience_configurations.csv  # (Generated by RDA.py) The core experience database for IDA decisions.
long_term_memory.note: SQLite Memory.db with experience configurations and user records persisted across runs.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: save snapshots of the user records to the Tables/User_Records/ directory
state_persistence.note: Snapshots written; no documented reload-and-continue path.

self_verification.evidence_quote: we further validate the pre-allocated bandwidth by measuring the empirical transmission rate under the proposed configuration before committing to the final assignment
self_verification.note: A numeric bandwidth verification step exists but matches none of the listed check types (not tests/lint/judge).

retry_policy.evidence_quote: the reallocation stage repeats until either sufficient idle bandwidth is secured (connected successfully) or no further adjustments are possible (connected failed)

rollback.evidence_quote: If reallocation can free up enough bandwidth for the new user, the IDA applies the changes and admits the new user. Otherwise, the access request is denied.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: until either sufficient idle bandwidth is secured (connected successfully) or no further adjustments are possible (connected failed)
termination_condition.note: Closest values: bandwidth verification pass = test_pass; 'no further adjustments possible' = stall_detection.

cost_controls.note: Per-call max_tokens only; no cost cap or caching.

execution_isolation.note: Simulation script runs in-process on host; no sandbox.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: Save the results to the path specified by experience_configuration_csv_file_path (i.e., Tables/Memory/experience_configurations.csv).
filesystem_access.note: Scripts read/write host filesystem; agent has no file tools.

permission_model.evidence_quote: the IDA applies the changes and admits the new user
permission_model.note: LLM-proposed configurations are applied after numeric verification; no authorisation layer.

tracing.evidence_quote: Log the entire process to the console and save snapshots of the user records to the Tables/User_Records/ directory.

replayability.evidence_quote: Log the entire process to the console and save snapshots of the user records to the Tables/User_Records/ directory.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: For each combination, evaluate the average bitstream length and task accuracy over the test set.
eval_hooks.note: RDA.py evaluation and RIDAS.py simulation reproduce the paper's experiments.

guardrails.evidence_quote: the LLM of IDA evaluates whether the configuration of any connected RDA can be adjusted to free up additional resources
guardrails.note: No safety filters or action policies present.

target_domain.evidence_quote: RIDAS is a novel multi-agent framework designed for AI-enabled Radio Access Networks (AI-RAN) in the 6G era.
